subject: Prefetch regeneration loop causing intermittent tail latency — escalation
messages:
From: Matthew Jackson <matthew.jackson@cerebrolabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: support@cerebrolabs.com
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: High tail latency from our prod cluster — urgent

Mina,

We're seeing repeated 95th/99th percentile spikes to 3-6s for generation requests intermittently across our service tier. Error rate also creeped from 0.3% to ~2.1% during the windows. The spikes correlate with large variance in per-request token counts, but looking at the traces it appears a large number of requests are hitting cache misses and then regenerating prefetch work which causes KV churn.

Attached is a short timeline I exported and a few sample traces. Our SLAs are at risk; our customers are experiencing timeouts. Can Redwood ops advise immediate mitigations (routing to more isolated capacity, temporary throttles, or config rollbacks)? We're open to scheduled maintenance but need a short-term fallback today.

Thanks,
Matt
Senior Platform Engineer
Cerebro Labs

Attachments: timeline.png (image)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Jackson <matthew.jackson@cerebrolabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High tail latency from our prod cluster — urgent

Matt — thanks for the timeline. I'm escalating this immediately to SRE and our performance leads. Initial read: the traces look like a prefetch regeneration feedback loop where prefix cache misses trigger large KV prefetches, which then evict hot keys and create head-of-line blocking on priority lanes. We have a few short mitigations we can try today:

- Temporarily pin Cerebro's requests to a reserved lane (minimize noisy neighbor effects)
- Reduce prefetch window size to limit aggressive KV churn
- Apply a conservative KV eviction policy (prefer LRU with weight on recent access)
- If necessary, failover a subset of traffic to a lower-capacity but isolated pool to protect SLAs

I'm looping in Ben and Jonas for immediate actions and a concrete rollback plan. Ben — can you review the suggested KV tweak (I attached a candidate diff) and stand by for a fast rollout? Jonas — can you coordinate reservations for an isolated lane and confirm capacity?

I'll update Matt once I have a runbook for a 30-min mitigation.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv-config.diff (patch)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 10:01:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High tail latency from our prod cluster — urgent

Quick notes after an initial config review:

- The current prefetch budget is set aggressively (window=1024 tokens, parallel=6) for this customer's workload shape. That combination is a known risk for regen loops when prefix distributions are heavy-tail.
- The KV eviction policy was recently changed to a frequency-biased sampler; that helps overall throughput but can be brittle for workloads with bursty prefixes.

Immediate plan (15-45 mins):
1) Roll the attached kv-config.diff to reduce prefetch window to 256 and parallel prefetchers to 2.
2) Revert eviction to time-weighted LRU for the affected pool.
3) Throttle Cerebro to 70% of usual QPS and pin to isolated pool while we observe for 30m.

I'll prepare a fast rollback and a canary gate. Rishi — can you prepare telemetry dashboards for kv miss rate, prefetch queue length, and lane headwaits so we can watch in real time?

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Jackson <matthew.jackson@cerebrolabs.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High tail latency from our prod cluster — urgent

Mina/Ben — I've reserved a 6x GPU lane in us-east-1 and pinned Cerebro traffic there. Traffic steering is in flight. Ben — please proceed with the smaller prefetch window and eviction change; I'll coordinate the throttle and isolate the pool.

Matt — we'll keep you updated every 15 minutes. For transparency: we may need to request a short SLA exception if reinstating aggressive prefetch is required later; we'll document changes and rollback criteria.

On the exec side, Evelyn — FYI. This is causing customer-visible timeouts; Cerebro is a mid-sized enterprise customer on an annual committed plan. We may need to offer a temporary credit if the window to full stabilization exceeds 4 hours.

Jonas
From: Matthew Jackson <matthew.jackson@cerebrolabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: support@cerebrolabs.com, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 11:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High tail latency from our prod cluster — urgent

Thanks for the quick response and plan. We're onboard with a temporary throttle and the isolated lane. Please keep the community traces flowing — the more telemetry we can see the quicker we can validate user impact. If the 30m observation shows improvement we'll gradually restore QPS.

One request: can Redwood share a short postmortem and the KV config diff after the incident? Our engineering leadership will want detailed notes for our risk review.

Matt
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Jackson <matthew.jackson@cerebrolabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 17:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High tail latency from our prod cluster — urgent

Update for the thread and execs:

- Actions taken: isolated Cerebro to reserved lane, reduced prefetch window to 256, parallel prefetchers to 2, and switched eviction to time-weighted LRU for the pool. Throttled to 70% QPS for 45 minutes during canary.
- Observed: within the first 12 minutes tail latency 99th dropped from ~5.2s to ~1.1s and error rate back to ~0.4%. Prefetch queue length and KV evictions dropped sharply.
- Next steps:
  * Keep isolated lane pinned for 24 hours while we collect telemetry.
  * Prepare a formal postmortem (root cause: aggressive prefetch + frequency-biased eviction produced a regeneration feedback loop that caused hot-key thrashing and head-of-line blocking on priority lanes).
  * Rishi will produce dashboards and a candidate mitigating config for longer-term tuning (adaptive prefetching, backpressure on prefetch queue, and per-tenant prefetch budgets).

Evelyn — we'll open a short SLA exception request (attached) and draft a customer-facing summary. Ben/Rishi/Jonas — please attach the rollout diffs and the quick-check list for the PM/SE teams.

Thanks everyone for the fast connect. Matt — expect the postmortem and a config bundle by EOD tomorrow.

— Mina
